subject: Post-call follow-up: RAG evaluation & retrieval + reranker tuning proposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call follow-up: RAG evaluation & retrieval + reranker tuning proposal

Hi Priya / Sentinel team,

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good alignment on the evaluation objectives. Below is a concise recap plus our proposed plan for the RAG evaluation and initial tuning recommendations.

Quick recap (from today):
- Goal: qualify Redwood-inference-backed RAG as a drop-in answer layer for clinical Q&A (focus on grounding precision and minimal hallucination).
- Data: ~120k docs (varied templates: policies, discharge notes, FAQs).
- Constraints: 99.9% PII redaction before indexing, 48-hr sync cadence for new content.
- Success metrics you emphasized: grounding_precision@1, hallucination_rate (per 1k responses), and average response latency under 600ms P50 for cached queries.

Initial model & eval recommendations (phase 1):
- Candidate LMs: RW-3-Chat-16k (high-efficiency production pick), Mistral-Instruct-7B (strong instruction-following baseline).
- Reranker: start with Redwood Neural Reranker v1 (cross-encoder pairwise) for top-8 re-ranking; plan to evaluate a lightweight bi-encoder rerank fallback for low-latency paths.
- Retriever: BM25 + dense-embedding hybrid. Offboard flow: BM25 top-200 then semantic embed top-50, final rerank top-8.

Retrieval & chunking suggestions to test:
- Doc chunk size: 600–1,000 tokens (keep clinical sections intact where possible).
- Chunk overlap: 120 tokens (roughly 20%–25%).
- Metadata filters: content_type (policy, note, faq) + source_date >= 2025-01-01 as a filter option.

Evaluation harness & prompts:
- We attached an initial benchmark sheet (sentinel_eval_benchmarks_v1.xlsx) with an initial set of 250 prompt+ground-truth pairs you shared.
- Shared Drive link with seed prompt sets and the canonical prompt templates is below.

Proposed next steps / timeline (phase 1):
1) We will run a two-week sweep across the candidate models + retriever configs: run automated metrics (grounding_precision@1, BLEU-like factuality, hallucination_rate) and human spot checks. (ETA: results by 2027-06-06)
2) Sync call to review top config and choose canary settings (1 hour).
3) If canary passes, deploy as a low-traffic canary with monitoring for 2 weeks.

Please confirm if this plan matches your priorities and whether we should add any additional checks (e.g., red-team prompts, safety filters).

Attachments: sentinel_eval_benchmarks_v1.xlsx (xlsx), prompt_set_seed_v1.md (md)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: RAG evaluation & retrieval + reranker tuning proposal

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we greenlight the two-week sweep: 

1) For the reranker you suggested (Redwood Neural Reranker v1), can you share expected latency/TPU-GPU footprint for cross-encoder inference when re-ranking top-8? We need a sense of cost and whether it can run in our Dedicated environment.
2) How are you planning to compute "grounding_precision@1" in the harness? Is that exact-match against a ground-truth span, or fuzzy (semantic) match?
3) We have a hard constraint on false positives for hallucination — can you provide an acceptance threshold that Redwood typically uses?

Also please share the evaluation harness (executable or notebook) so our SRE can vet resource requirements.

Last — can we add a small set (n=30) of "high-stakes" prompts to the seed set (we'll send them this afternoon)?

- Priya
Senior Product Manager, Clinical Search | Sentinel Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: RAG evaluation & retrieval + reranker tuning proposal

Priya — great questions. Answers below and an operational plan to address each item.

1) Reranker latency / footprint:
- Redwood Neural Reranker v1 (cross-encoder) typical runtime for top-8 re-rank: ~18–45ms per query on an A10G-style GPU with batch fusion (depends on batch size / KV-cache).
- CPU-only is possible with larger latency (~150–300ms) but we recommend GPU for production canary.
- For Dedicated customers we provide a recommended instance profile (2x A10G per 100 qps for cross-encoder heavy workloads) and a low-cost fallback (bi-encoder + small re-rank model) for lower tiers.

2) grounding_precision@1 methodology:
- Primary metric: semantic-span overlap (token-level F1 vs. annotated ground-truth span) with a thresholded match (F1 >= 0.7 counts as grounded).
- Secondary metric: presence_of_support_score — whether the returned top chunk contains an explicit citation match. We report both; grounding_precision@1 is defined as percent of queries where top returned answer meets the F1 threshold.

3) hallucination acceptance threshold:
- Our baseline recommendation: initial canary acceptance if hallucination_rate <= 12 per 1k responses AND grounding_precision@1 >= 0.88.
- For clinical high-stakes content we suggest tightening to <= 6 per 1k and grounding_precision@1 >= 0.92 after additional tuning and reranker fine-tuning.

Operational items we will deliver by EOD Monday (2027-05-24):
- Evaluation harness (Jupyter notebook + Dockerfile) with scripts to reproduce metrics and resource profiling.
- Updated benchmark sheet with expected output columns (ground-truth span, F1, presence_of_support_score, model_resp_latency).
- Prompt-set folder in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/sentinel/rag-eval/prompt-set-v1 (we put the seed prompts and a README describing mixing strategy for human eval).

Retrieval config we will test in the sweep (details):
- Phase A (fast): BM25 top-200, chunk_size=800 tokens, overlap=120, top_k_semantic=12, final_rerank_top=8.
- Phase B (high-fidelity): BM25 top-500 + dense-recall on FAISS (128-d) top-100, reduce chunk_size to 600 for denser contexts, rerank_top=8 with cross-encoder.

Reranker training notes:
- If you can provide labeled pairs (good/bad candidate for ~3k examples), we can fine-tune a pairwise reranker before the canary. If not, we will start with the Redwood Neural Reranker v1 (pretrained) and compare it to an off-the-shelf cross-encoder.

Next steps:
- Please upload the 30 high-stakes prompts to the shared drive (we'll segregate them as the "safety set").
- We will send the evaluation harness + Dockerfile link in a separate email and schedule a quick SRE call to review resource needs.

CC'ing Laura and Ben so they can flag any infra constraints or additional tests to include.

Thanks — Marcus
